# Buy-Till-You-Die models (Pareto/NBD, BG/NBD): assumptions and data requirements

## Sources (primary, working URLs)

- **Fader, P.S., Hardie, B.G.S., Lee, K.L. (2005).** "'Counting Your Customers' the Easy Way: An Alternative to the Pareto/NBD Model." *Marketing Science* 24(2): 275-284. Author's working-paper PDF (Aug 2003, rev. April 2004), fetched and read directly: https://www.brucehardie.com/papers/bgnbd_2004-04-20.pdf (published version: https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mksc.1040.0098)
- **Schmittlein, D.C., Morrison, D.G., Colombo, R. (1987).** "Counting Your Customers: Who Are They and What Will They Do Next?" *Management Science* 33(1): 1-24. (Publisher page: https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.33.1.1). I did **not** obtain the SMC 1987 full text directly (paywalled); the Pareto/NBD assumptions below are quoted as **restated in Fader/Hardie/Lee 2005**, which is itself a primary source in the same modeling tradition and explicitly attributes the framework to "Schmittlein, Morrison, and Colombo (1987)... hereafter SMC." I flag this rather than fabricate SMC page/quote content.
- Companion technical note "A Step-by-Step Derivation of the BG/NBD Model": http://www.brucehardie.com/notes/039/ (located via search; not separately fetched — the 2005 paper already contains the full derivation).

All quotations below are transcribed from the PDF pages I read directly.

---

## 1. Modeling assumptions

### Pareto/NBD — five assumptions (verbatim, Fader/Hardie/Lee §2, p. 2, restating SMC 1987)

> "The Pareto/NBD model is based on five assumptions:
> i. While active, the number of transactions made by a customer in a time period of length *t* is distributed Poisson with transaction rate λ.
> ii. Heterogeneity in transaction rates across customers follows a gamma distribution with shape parameter *r* and scale parameter α.
> iii. Each customer has an unobserved 'lifetime' of length τ. This point at which the customer becomes inactive is distributed exponential with dropout rate μ.
> iv. Heterogeneity in dropout rates across customers follows a gamma distribution with shape parameter *s* and scale parameter β.
> v. The transaction rate λ and the dropout rate μ vary independently across customers."

This confirms every element of the claim in the task: (a) Poisson purchasing while active with rate λ; (b) λ ~ gamma across customers; (c) exponential unobserved lifetime with dropout rate μ (the "Pareto" name comes from the exponential-gamma mixture — introduction, p. 1: "time to 'dropout' is modelled using the Pareto (exponential-gamma mixture) timing model, and repeat-buying behavior while active is modelled using the NBD (Poisson-gamma mixture) counting model"); (d) μ ~ gamma; (e) λ and μ independent. All sourced, none inferred.

### BG/NBD — five assumptions (verbatim, §3, pp. 4-5)

The paper first states the single conceptual difference (§3, p. 4):

> "The only difference lies in the story being told about how/when customers become inactive. The Pareto timing model assumes that dropout can occur at any point in time, independent of the occurrence of actual purchases. If we assume instead that dropout occurs immediately after a purchase, we can model this process using the beta-geometric (BG) model."

The five assumptions (first two identical to Pareto/NBD):

> "i. While active, the number of transactions made by a customer follows a Poisson process with transaction rate λ. This is equivalent to assuming that the time between transactions is distributed exponential with transaction rate λ...
> ii. Heterogeneity in λ follows a gamma distribution with pdf [gamma, parameters *r*, α]...
> iii. After any transaction, a customer becomes inactive with probability *p*. Therefore the point at which the customer 'drops out' is distributed across transactions according to a (shifted) geometric distribution with pmf: P(inactive immediately after *j*th transaction) = *p*(1−*p*)^(*j*−1), *j* = 1, 2, 3, ....
> iv. Heterogeneity in *p* follows a beta distribution with pdf [beta, parameters *a*, *b*]...
> v. The transaction rate λ and the dropout probability *p* vary independently across customers."

This confirms the task's BG variant description exactly: dropout is a **beta-geometric process** — the customer becomes inactive with probability *p* **immediately after each transaction** (dropout can occur only right after a purchase, not at an arbitrary time), and *p* ~ beta. A consequence the paper notes (§4.3, p. 7): under BG/NBD the dropout process has "an explicit association with the transaction rate λ, in contrast with the Pareto/NBD, which has an exponential dropout process that is independent of the transaction rate."

---

## 2. Required per-customer summary statistics (recency, frequency, T)

Stated explicitly (§2, p. 3):

> "The Pareto/NBD (and, as we will see shortly, the BG/NBD) requires only two pieces of information about each customer's past purchasing history: his 'recency' (when his last transaction occurred) and 'frequency' (how many transactions he made in a specified time period). The notation used to represent this information is (*X* = *x*, *t_x*, *T*), where *x* is the number of transactions observed in the time period (0, *T*] and *t_x* (0 < *t_x* ≤ *T*) is the time of the last transaction."

And that the exact timing of intermediate transactions is **not** needed — only the recency/frequency/T triple is sufficient (§4.1, p. 6):

> "note that information on the timing of the *x* transactions is not required; a sufficient summary of the customer's purchase history is (*X* = *x*, *t_x*, *T*)."

**Repeat transactions specifically.** The models describe **repeat**-buying behavior (introduction, p. 1: SMC "describes repeat-buying behavior"). The empirical section makes the repeat framing concrete (§7, p. 12):

> "We calibrate the model using the repeat transaction data for the 2357 sampled customers over the first half of the 78-week period... For customer *i*..., we know the length of the time period during which repeat transactions could have occurred (*T_i* = 39 − time of first purchase), the number of repeat transactions in this period (*x_i*) and the time of his last repeat transaction (*t_xi*). (If *x_i* = 0, *t_xi* = 0.)"

So *T* is measured from the initial (trial) purchase, and *x*, *t_x* count **repeat** transactions only. Customers enter the model as active at their first purchase (§4.1, p. 6: "we assume that all customers are active at the beginning of the observation period"). This confirms the task's point that the models require repeat-purchase histories.

---

## 3. Need for a sufficiently long / informative observation window

The paper documents where these models **degrade**, and it is precisely the sparse-data / low-repeat regime (§6 simulation, p. 11):

> "the BG/NBD forecasts tend to be relatively poor when penetration and/or purchase frequency are extremely low."

The reported contrast (Table 1, p. 11): the "Worst 10 worlds" had penetration 18.8 % and **average purchase frequency 1.2**, with MAPE 5.73; the other 71 worlds had penetration 44.5 %, average frequency 3.9, MAPE 2.26. The mechanism is stated (p. 11):

> "in a world where active buyers are either uncommon or very slow in making their purchases, the Pareto/NBD will tend to outperform the BG/NBD."

The paper also urges monitoring these very statistics (p. 11): "we encourage managers to continually monitor summary statistics such as penetration and purchase frequency."

Interpretation grounded in the source: the dropout/lifetime process is **unobserved** and is inferred entirely from the count and spacing of **repeat** purchases within (0, *T*]. When average purchase frequency is near 1 (few or no repeat transactions per customer) the recency-frequency statistics carry little signal to separate "has become inactive" from "still active but has not purchased again yet," and fit/forecast quality falls off. This is the documented data requirement: enough observation time and enough repeat transactions for the interpurchase-time and dropout processes to be estimable. (The specific phrasing "unstable/unidentified parameters" is **not** a verbatim claim in this paper; what the paper documents verbatim is degraded forecast accuracy under low penetration/low frequency, which is the empirical manifestation. I mark the identification-language as a reasonable paraphrase, not a direct quote.)

Additional context on estimation difficulty (§2, p. 3): the Pareto/NBD likelihood is "quite complex, involving numerous evaluations of the Gaussian hypergeometric function," which "can cause major problems for numerical optimization routines" — this is why BG/NBD was created, and is separate from the sparse-data issue above.

---

## 4. Applicability inference: customer-level, not customer-PRODUCT (clearly marked as MY inference)

**This section is applicability inference, not a claim made in the source.** The papers never discuss a customer-product matrix.

What the sources *do* establish (all cited above): the unit of analysis is the **customer** (or customer relationship) observed in **continuous time**, and the entire estimable signal comes from the **count and recency of repeat transactions** per customer over an observation window *T* — the sufficient statistic (*x*, *t_x*, *T*). The dropout process is inferred from the spacing/recency of those repeat events.

The grounded inference: a **saturated customer-product matrix with (at most) one transaction per customer-product cell** provides no repeat-purchase timing signal at the cell level. Per cell, *x* ≤ 1 and there is no interpurchase interval, so *t_x* and the recency-vs-not-yet-repurchased distinction collapse — the RFM sufficient statistics degenerate exactly into the "extremely low purchase frequency" regime the paper flags as where the model performs worst (avg. frequency ≈ 1). BG/NBD's dropout assumption ("inactive with probability *p* after each transaction") also cannot be identified from at most one transaction. These BTYD models are therefore appropriate at the **customer / customer-relationship** grain across all purchases, not at the **customer-product** grain of a one-transaction-per-cell matrix. This conclusion follows from the models' stated sufficient statistics and their documented low-frequency failure mode, but the papers themselves do not address the customer-product case — treat it as reasoned applicability inference.

---

## Sourced-vs-inferred summary

- Assumptions (Pareto/NBD and BG/NBD), the beta-geometric "dropout only right after a purchase" distinction, the (*x*, *t_x*, *T*) sufficient statistics, the "only repeat transactions" framing, and the low-penetration/low-frequency degradation: **all directly sourced and quoted** from Fader/Hardie/Lee (2005).
- Pareto/NBD five assumptions: sourced from Fader/Hardie/Lee's restatement of SMC (1987); **SMC 1987 not fetched directly** (paywalled) — flagged.
- "Unstable/unidentified parameters under short/sparse data": **paraphrase** of the documented forecast-degradation finding, not a verbatim claim.
- Customer-level vs. customer-product applicability and the degenerate one-transaction-per-cell matrix: **my applicability inference**, grounded in the models' stated data requirements, not asserted by the sources.

## Verification report: empirical CCDF vs. Kaplan-Meier under right-censoring

### 1. Kaplan & Meier (1958) — full citation and the problem it solves

**Citation:** Kaplan, E.L. and Meier, P. (1958), "Nonparametric Estimation from Incomplete Observations," *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 53(282), 457-481.

**Abstract (verbatim, retrieved via search index of JASA abstract):**
> "In lifetesting, medical follow-up, and other fields the observation of the time of occurrence of the event of interest (called a death) may be prevented for some of the items of the sample by the previous occurrence of some other event (called a loss). Losses may be either accidental or controlled... In either case it is usually assumed in this paper that the lifetime (age at death) is independent of the potential loss time. Despite the resulting incompleteness of the data, it is desired to estimate the proportion P(t) of items in the population whose lifetimes would exceed t (in the absence of such losses), without making any assumption about the form of the function P(t)."

This directly states points 1 and 3 of the task: it is a **nonparametric** estimator (no assumed form for P(t)) of the survival function from **incomplete (censored) observations**, and it explicitly assumes **lifetime is independent of the loss (censoring) time** — the non-informative censoring assumption. The estimator's purpose is to recover P(t) despite items whose event time was not observed, rather than discarding them.

Note on sourcing: I could not extract the abstract from the full-text PDF (Stanford host: `web.stanford.edu/~lutian/coursepdf/KMpaper.pdf` — the file is FlateDecode-compressed binary and did not render as text). ### 2. Documented caution: the naive empirical estimator is biased downward under right-censoring

Authoritative secondary confirmation from the **lifelines** documentation (Cameron Davidson-Pilon; the canonical Python survival-analysis library), "Introduction to Survival Analysis" page:

- Verbatim: *"A common mistake data analysts make is choosing to ignore the right-censored individuals."*
- Paraphrase (closely tracking the source text): if one naively decides to **not** include the right-censored individuals, one would be **severely underestimating the true average lifespan**.
- Verbatim: *"if we instead simply took the mean of all lifespans, including the current lifespans of right-censored instances, we would still be underestimating the true average lifespan."*

This confirms point 2 in both forms: whether censored/ongoing durations are dropped, **or** counted as if completed, the naive empirical result **underestimates survival / long durations**. The mechanism is that subjects still "alive"/ongoing at the cutoff have not yet reached their event, so their observed duration is a lower bound, not the event time.

Supporting statement (research literature, arXiv 1310.5927): "the empirical cdf does not provide a consistent estimator of the cdf in the presence of censored data," and "the cdf can be consistently estimated by the Kaplan-Meier estimator... which generalizes the empirical cdf to the censored case." I flag this as a secondary/peer-reviewed-preprint source, not a textbook.

### 3. Why Kaplan-Meier is the correct nonparametric estimator (product-limit / risk sets)

NIST/SEMATECH *Engineering Statistics Handbook* (apr215.htm), verbatim:
- *"The Kaplan-Meier (K-M) Product Limit procedure provides quick, simple estimates of the Reliability function or the CDF based on failure data that may even be multicensored."*
- On correct use of the risk set: *"Unfailed units taken off test (i.e., censored) only count up to the last actual failure time before they were removed. They are included in the n_i counts up to and including that failure time, but not after."*

This is the product-limit construction: at each observed event time the estimate is multiplied by (1 − d_i/n_i), where n_i is the **risk set** (units still under observation at that time); censored units contribute to n_i until their censoring time, then leave. This is exactly the mechanism that a naive empirical CCDF lacks.

Klein, J.P. and Moeschberger, M.L. (2003), *Survival Analysis: Techniques for Censored and Truncated Data*, 2nd ed., Springer (ISBN 038795399X) is the standard textbook reference for this estimator being the de facto standard under partial right-censoring. I confirmed the citation and the book's scope but was **unable to retrieve a verbatim in-text quote** from it (no accessible full text); I flag the specific page/quote as unverified.

### 4. Cautions about Kaplan-Meier itself

**(a) Right-tail instability / improper estimate when the largest observation is censored.**
NIST handbook, verbatim: *"The K-M estimate at the time of the last failure is R(t_r) = 0 and F(t_r) = 1. This estimate has a pessimistic bias and cannot be plotted (without modification)..."* — this is the case where the largest time is a failure. The complementary caution, from the survival-extremes literature (arXiv 2103.01337, 2002.11239): when the **largest observation is censored**, "the sample Kaplan-Meier estimator becomes improper, i.e., of total mass less than 1," levelling off "below 1 at the right hand end," and the survival function is **undefined below that plateau beyond the largest observed time**. So the right tail is either driven to 0 (last event) or left undefined above the plateau (last time censored) — unstable/undefined either way.

**(b) Non-informative (independent) censoring assumption.**
Stated directly in the KM (1958) abstract itself ("the lifetime... is independent of the potential loss time"). This is the core assumption: censoring must be independent of the event process, or the estimate is biased.

### Recommendation (as documented in the sources)

Under right-censoring, use the **Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator**, not the naive empirical CCDF. The naive empirical survival/CCDF is a biased, inconsistent estimator that systematically underestimates survival (overstates the event rate / understates long durations) because ongoing subjects at the cutoff are treated as completed or dropped. If the empirical CCDF is being used specifically as a decay *weight*, the same bias applies: durations near and beyond the observation window are under-weighted. Caveats when adopting KM: it assumes non-informative/independent censoring, and its right tail is unstable (driven to 0 at a terminal event) or undefined (plateau above the last censored time), so weights derived from the extreme tail are unreliable.

## 1. A composite rank is NOT a robust number — it depends on subjective choices

Handbook, §1.7 (p. 34), verbatim: *"Several judgements have to be made when constructing composite indicators, e.g. on the selection of indicators, data normalisation, weights and aggregation methods, etc. The robustness of the composite indicators and the underlying policy messages may thus be contested."*

Saisana et al. (2005) abstract, verbatim: *"Composite indicators are increasingly used for bench-marking countries' performances. Yet doubts are often raised about the robustness of the resulting countries' rankings and about the significance of the associated policy message."*

The Handbook explicitly enumerates the uncertainty sources to vary (p. 34): inclusion/exclusion of indicators; data-error modelling; alternative imputation; alternative normalisation (Min-Max, standardisation, rankings); different weighting schemes; different aggregation systems; different plausible weight values. The TAI case concludes bluntly (p. 124): *"it would have to be concluded that TAI is not a robust measure of countries' technology achievement."*

## 2. Monte Carlo / multi-modelling → report the RANGE of ranks; variance-based (Sobol) SA to attribute rank variance

# Verification report: compensatory vs non-compensatory aggregation (primary sources)

All quotes below are transcribed verbatim from the source PDFs (I read the pages directly, not a summarizer). Page numbers are the **printed page numbers** shown in each page footer.

## Source A (primary) — the Handbook

**Full citation:** Nardo, M., Saisana, M., Saltelli, A., Tarantola, S., Hoffman, A., Giovannini, E. (2008). *Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide*. OECD Publishing / European Commission Joint Research Centre. ISBN 978-92-64-04345-9.
**Working URL (official PDF):** https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2008/08/handbook-on-constructing-composite-indicators-methodology-and-user-guide_g1gh9301/9789264043466-en.pdf
JRC repository: https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC47008

Note on structure: the relevant material appears twice — a condensed treatment in the Executive Summary §1.6 "Weighting and aggregation" (printed pp. 31–33) and the detailed treatment in Step 6 §6.10 "Additive aggregation methods", §6.11 "Geometric aggregation" and §6.12 (printed pp. 99–108).

### 1. Additive/linear aggregation implies FULL compensability (verified quotes)

- (§6.11, p. 103) "As discussed above, an undesirable feature of additive aggregations is the implied **full compensability**, such that poor performance in some indicators can be compensated for by sufficiently high values in other indicators."
- (§1.6, p. 33) "In both linear and geometric aggregations, weights express trade-offs between indicators. A **deficit in one dimension can thus be offset (compensated) by a surplus in another.** … In a linear aggregation, the **compensability is constant**, while with geometric aggregations compensability is lower for the composite indicators with low values."
- Formal basis (§6.10, p. 103): a linear additive function requires "**preference independence**", which the Handbook calls "a very strong condition, as it implies that the trade-off ratio between two variables … is independent of the values of the … other variables". It adds that assuming "no synergies or conflicts … appears to be quite an unrealistic assumption (Funtowicz et al., 1990)", citing the example that combined acidifying substances harm plants far more than the linear sum of their separate impacts.

### 2. Geometric aggregation — partial (reduced) compensability, rewards balance

- (§1.6, p. 32) "Geometric aggregations are better suited if the modeller wants **some degree of non compensability** between individual indicators or dimensions."
- (§1.6, p. 33) "linear aggregations reward base-indicators proportionally to the weights, while **geometric aggregations reward those countries with higher scores**."
- Worked example (§6.11, p. 104): two profiles [21,1,1,1] and [6,6,6,6] give **equal** additive composites but geometric scores of **2.14 vs 6** — the balanced profile scores far higher. The Handbook notes "countries with low scores in some individual indicators … would prefer a linear rather than a geometric aggregation" and that geometric gives "a greater incentive to address those sectors/activities/alternatives with low scores".

**Sensitivity to zero / positivity requirement — HONEST CAVEAT.** I did NOT find a single verbatim Handbook sentence stating "the geometric mean is zero if any component is zero." That is a mathematical property of the product form CI = Πₓ xᵩ^wᵩ (the geometric formula printed on p. 104), not an explicitly quoted caution in this text. What the Handbook does document nearby: Min-Max normalization maps the laggard exactly to **0** and the leader to 1 (§5.3, p. 85: "values lying between 0 (laggard …) and 1 (leader …)"). The combination — a product aggregation over min-max values that can equal 0 — is what makes the zero-sensitivity operative, but the reader must connect those two statements; the Handbook does not spell it out in one quotable caution. (The widely cited canonical statement of this zero-value problem is in the UNDP Human Development Report 2010 technical notes, which switched the HDI to a geometric mean — a different primary source, not verified here.)

### 3. Interpretability trade-offs (verified)

- Linear: "simple", intuitive when indicators share a measurement unit, but "imposes restrictions on the nature of individual indicators" and can yield "a biased composite indicator … [whose] dimension and … direction of the error are not easily determined" (§6.10, p. 103).
- Geometric: harder to interpret as a simple sum; rewards higher/balanced scores non-proportionally.
- Non-compensatory MCA (§1.6, p. 33): "In its basic form this approach **does not reward outliers, as it retains only ordinal information** … This method, however, **could be computationally costly** when the number of countries is high, as the number of permutations to calculate increases exponentially (Munda & Nardo, 2007)."

### 4. WEIGHTS are trade-off ratios, NOT importance coefficients (the key documented misinterpretation) — verified

- **Table 4, footnote 4 (p. 31), verbatim:** "**With both linear and geometric aggregations weights are trade-offs and not 'importance' coefficients.**"
- Table 4, footnote 3 (p. 31): "At least with the multi-criteria methods requiring weights **as importance coefficients**."
- (§1.6, p. 33) "This implies an **inconsistency between how weights are conceived (usually measuring the importance of the associated variable) and the actual meaning when geometric or linear aggregations are used.** … To ensure that weights remain a measure of importance, other aggregation methods should be used, in particular methods that do not allow compensability."
- The decisive formal statement (§6.12, p. 105): "The use of weights with **intensity of preference** originates in **compensatory** multi-criteria methods and gives the meaning of **trade-offs** to the weights. By contrast, the use of weights with **ordinal criterion scores** originates in **non-compensatory** aggregation procedures and gives the weights the meaning of **importance coefficients** (Keeney & Raiffa, 1976; Podinovskii, 1994; Roberts, 1979)."

### 5. Non-compensatory MCA as the correct choice for non-substitutable dimensions (Handbook view)

- (§1.6, p. 33) "if different goals are **equally legitimate and important, a non-compensatory logic might be necessary**. This is usually the case when highly different dimensions are aggregated … as in the case of environmental indices … where the analyst decides that an increase in economic performance cannot compensate for a loss in social cohesion or a worsening in environmental sustainability, then neither the linear nor the geometric aggregation are suitable. A non-compensatory multi-criteria approach (MCA) could assure non-compensability by finding a compromise between two or more legitimate goals."
- Cost, via Arrow (§6.12, p. 105): Arrow & Raynaud (1986) "proved that the correct solution of a multi-criterion problem comes from a mono-criterion optimisation. A consequence of this theorem is that **no perfect aggregation rule may exist.** '"Reasonable" ranking procedures must therefore be found.'" The Handbook then develops Condorcet/Borda voting procedures (pp. 106–108) as the non-compensatory ranking machinery.

## Source B (primary) — Munda & Nardo

**Full citation:** Munda, G. & Nardo, M. (2009). "Noncompensatory/nonlinear composite indicators for ranking countries: a defensible setting." *Applied Economics*, 41(12), 1513–1523. DOI: 10.1080/00036840601019364.
- Journal record: https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00036840601019364 and https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/applec/v41y2009i12p1513-1523.html
- Earlier JRC working-paper version: Munda, G. & Nardo, M. (2005). *Non-Compensatory/Non-Linear Composite Indicators for Ranking Countries: A Defensible Setting.* EUR 21833 EN, European Commission JRC. PDF: https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/bitstream/JRC32435/EUR%2021833%20EN.pdf (repository handle: https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC34883)

**Abstract (verbatim, from the RePEc/Applied Economics record):** "… This article aims at contributing to the improvement of the overall quality of composite indicators … by looking at one of their technical weaknesses, that is, the **aggregation convention** used for their construction. For this aim, we build upon concepts coming from **multi-criteria decision analysis, measurement theory and social choice.** We start from the analysis of the axiomatic system underlying the mathematical modelling commonly used … Then a different methodological framework, based on **noncompensatory/nonlinear aggregation rules,** is developed. Main features … are: (i) the axiomatic system is made completely explicit and (ii) the sources of technical uncertainty and imprecise assessment are reduced to the minimum possible degree."

**Verification caveat on Source B:** WebFetch could not extract the body text of the JRC EUR 21833 PDF (encoding/compression garble), so I could not transcribe verbatim page-level quotes from Munda & Nardo's own text. What is firmly established: (a) the citation and abstract above are verified; (b) the Handbook's entire §6.12 argument — Arrow's impossibility, the Borda/Condorcet ranking procedures, the ordinal (importance-coefficient) reading of weights, and the "computationally costly … permutations increase exponentially" caveat — is explicitly attributed to Munda & Nardo (2005; 2007) and G. Munda, and is therefore a faithful secondary channel of their argument. Their thesis, as reflected there: when criteria/dimensions are **non-substitutable**, compensatory (additive/geometric) aggregation is axiomatically inappropriate; the defensible alternative is a non-compensatory multi-criteria/Condorcet-type rule that uses only ordinal information and treats weights as importance coefficients — at the documented cost that no perfect aggregation rule exists (Arrow), rankings can exhibit Condorcet-style cycles, and the combinatorial computation grows with the number of alternatives.

## Bottom line for the caller
Every claim in the topic statement is **corroborated by the Handbook's own text** with the quotes above, with two honesty flags: (1) the "geometric mean = 0 if any component is 0" caution is a mathematical property the Handbook implies (product form + min-max lower bound of 0) but does not state as a single quotable sentence; the canonical explicit statement lives in the UNDP HDR 2010 (not verified here). (2) Munda & Nardo's own wording could not be quoted verbatim from the JRC PDF, but their citation/abstract are verified and their argument is faithfully carried in Handbook §6.12.

**Full citation:** Nardo, M., Saisana, M., Saltelli, A., Tarantola, S., Hoffman, A., Giovannini, E. (2008). *Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide*. OECD Publishing / European Commission Joint Research Centre. ISBN 978-92-64-04345-9.
**Working URL (official PDF):** https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2008/08/handbook-on-constructing-composite-indicators-methodology-and-user-guide_g1gh9301/9789264043466-en.pdf
JRC repository: https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC47008

Note on structure: the relevant material appears twice — a condensed treatment in the Executive Summary §1.6 "Weighting and aggregation" (printed pp. 31–33) and the detailed treatment in Step 6 §6.10 "Additive aggregation methods", §6.11 "Geometric aggregation" and §6.12 (printed pp. 99–108).

### 1. Additive/linear aggregation implies FULL compensability (verified quotes)

- (§6.11, p. 103) "As discussed above, an undesirable feature of additive aggregations is the implied **full compensability**, such that poor performance in some indicators can be compensated for by sufficiently high values in other indicators."
- (§1.6, p. 33) "In both linear and geometric aggregations, weights express trade-offs between indicators. A **deficit in one dimension can thus be offset (compensated) by a surplus in another.** … In a linear aggregation, the **compensability is constant**, while with geometric aggregations compensability is lower for the composite indicators with low values."
- Formal basis (§6.10, p. 103): a linear additive function requires "**preference independence**", which the Handbook calls "a very strong condition, as it implies that the trade-off ratio between two variables … is independent of the values of the … other variables". It adds that assuming "no synergies or conflicts … appears to be quite an unrealistic assumption (Funtowicz et al., 1990)", citing the example that combined acidifying substances harm plants far more than the linear sum of their separate impacts.

### 2. Geometric aggregation — partial (reduced) compensability, rewards balance

- (§1.6, p. 32) "Geometric aggregations are better suited if the modeller wants **some degree of non compensability** between individual indicators or dimensions."
- (§1.6, p. 33) "linear aggregations reward base-indicators proportionally to the weights, while **geometric aggregations reward those countries with higher scores**."
- Worked example (§6.11, p. 104): two profiles [21,1,1,1] and [6,6,6,6] give **equal** additive composites but geometric scores of **2.14 vs 6** — the balanced profile scores far higher. The Handbook notes "countries with low scores in some individual indicators … would prefer a linear rather than a geometric aggregation" and that geometric gives "a greater incentive to address those sectors/activities/alternatives with low scores".

**Sensitivity to zero / positivity requirement — HONEST CAVEAT.** I did NOT find a single verbatim Handbook sentence stating "the geometric mean is zero if any component is zero." That is a mathematical property of the product form CI = Πₓ xᵩ^wᵩ (the geometric formula printed on p. 104), not an explicitly quoted caution in this text. What the Handbook does document nearby: Min-Max normalization maps the laggard exactly to **0** and the leader to 1 (§5.3, p. 85: "values lying between 0 (laggard …) and 1 (leader …)"). The combination — a product aggregation over min-max values that can equal 0 — is what makes the zero-sensitivity operative, but the reader must connect those two statements; the Handbook does not spell it out in one quotable caution. (The widely cited canonical statement of this zero-value problem is in the UNDP Human Development Report 2010 technical notes, which switched the HDI to a geometric mean — a different primary source, not verified here.)

### 3. Interpretability trade-offs (verified)

- Linear: "simple", intuitive when indicators share a measurement unit, but "imposes restrictions on the nature of individual indicators" and can yield "a biased composite indicator … [whose] dimension and … direction of the error are not easily determined" (§6.10, p. 103).
- Geometric: harder to interpret as a simple sum; rewards higher/balanced scores non-proportionally.
- Non-compensatory MCA (§1.6, p. 33): "In its basic form this approach **does not reward outliers, as it retains only ordinal information** … This method, however, **could be computationally costly** when the number of countries is high, as the number of permutations to calculate increases exponentially (Munda & Nardo, 2007)."

### 4. WEIGHTS are trade-off ratios, NOT importance coefficients (the key documented misinterpretation) — verified

- **Table 4, footnote 4 (p. 31), verbatim:** "**With both linear and geometric aggregations weights are trade-offs and not 'importance' coefficients.**"
- Table 4, footnote 3 (p. 31): "At least with the multi-criteria methods requiring weights **as importance coefficients**."
- (§1.6, p. 33) "This implies an **inconsistency between how weights are conceived (usually measuring the importance of the associated variable) and the actual meaning when geometric or linear aggregations are used.** … To ensure that weights remain a measure of importance, other aggregation methods should be used, in particular methods that do not allow compensability."
- The decisive formal statement (§6.12, p. 105): "The use of weights with **intensity of preference** originates in **compensatory** multi-criteria methods and gives the meaning of **trade-offs** to the weights. By contrast, the use of weights with **ordinal criterion scores** originates in **non-compensatory** aggregation procedures and gives the weights the meaning of **importance coefficients** (Keeney & Raiffa, 1976; Podinovskii, 1994; Roberts, 1979)."

### 5. Non-compensatory MCA as the correct choice for non-substitutable dimensions (Handbook view)

- (§1.6, p. 33) "if different goals are **equally legitimate and important, a non-compensatory logic might be necessary**. This is usually the case when highly different dimensions are aggregated … as in the case of environmental indices … where the analyst decides that an increase in economic performance cannot compensate for a loss in social cohesion or a worsening in environmental sustainability, then neither the linear nor the geometric aggregation are suitable. A non-compensatory multi-criteria approach (MCA) could assure non-compensability by finding a compromise between two or more legitimate goals."
- Cost, via Arrow (§6.12, p. 105): Arrow & Raynaud (1986) "proved that the correct solution of a multi-criterion problem comes from a mono-criterion optimisation. A consequence of this theorem is that **no perfect aggregation rule may exist.** '"Reasonable" ranking procedures must therefore be found.'" The Handbook then develops Condorcet/Borda voting procedures (pp. 106–108) as the non-compensatory ranking machinery.

## Source B (primary) — Munda & Nardo

**Full citation:** Munda, G. & Nardo, M. (2009). "Noncompensatory/nonlinear composite indicators for ranking countries: a defensible setting." *Applied Economics*, 41(12), 1513–1523. DOI: 10.1080/00036840601019364.
- Journal record: https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00036840601019364 and https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/applec/v41y2009i12p1513-1523.html
- Earlier JRC working-paper version: Munda, G. & Nardo, M. (2005). *Non-Compensatory/Non-Linear Composite Indicators for Ranking Countries: A Defensible Setting.* EUR 21833 EN, European Commission JRC. PDF: https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/bitstream/JRC32435/EUR%2021833%20EN.pdf (repository handle: https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC34883)

**Abstract (verbatim, from the RePEc/Applied Economics record):** "… This article aims at contributing to the improvement of the overall quality of composite indicators … by looking at one of their technical weaknesses, that is, the **aggregation convention** used for their construction. For this aim, we build upon concepts coming from **multi-criteria decision analysis, measurement theory and social choice.** We start from the analysis of the axiomatic system underlying the mathematical modelling commonly used … Then a different methodological framework, based on **noncompensatory/nonlinear aggregation rules,** is developed. Main features … are: (i) the axiomatic system is made completely explicit and (ii) the sources of technical uncertainty and imprecise assessment are reduced to the minimum possible degree."

**Verification caveat on Source B:** WebFetch could not extract the body text of the JRC EUR 21833 PDF (encoding/compression garble), so I could not transcribe verbatim page-level quotes from Munda & Nardo's own text. What is firmly established: (a) the citation and abstract above are verified; (b) the Handbook's entire §6.12 argument — Arrow's impossibility, the Borda/Condorcet ranking procedures, the ordinal (importance-coefficient) reading of weights, and the "computationally costly … permutations increase exponentially" caveat — is explicitly attributed to Munda & Nardo (2005; 2007) and G. Munda, and is therefore a faithful secondary channel of their argument. Their thesis, as reflected there: when criteria/dimensions are **non-substitutable**, compensatory (additive/geometric) aggregation is axiomatically inappropriate; the defensible alternative is a non-compensatory multi-criteria/Condorcet-type rule that uses only ordinal information and treats weights as importance coefficients — at the documented cost that no perfect aggregation rule exists (Arrow), rankings can exhibit Condorcet-style cycles, and the combinatorial computation grows with the number of alternatives.

## Bottom line for the caller
Every claim in the topic statement is **corroborated by the Handbook's own text** with the quotes above, with two honesty flags: (1) the "geometric mean = 0 if any component is 0" caution is a mathematical property the Handbook implies (product form + min-max lower bound of 0) but does not state as a single quotable sentence; the canonical explicit statement lives in the UNDP HDR 2010 (not verified here). (2) Munda & Nardo's own wording could not be quoted verbatim from the JRC PDF, but their citation/abstract are verified and their argument is faithfully carried in Handbook §6.12.

Sources:
- [OECD/JRC Handbook 2008 (PDF)](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2008/08/handbook-on-constructing-composite-indicators-methodology-and-user-guide_g1gh9301/9789264043466-en.pdf)
- [Munda & Nardo 2009, Applied Economics (RePEc)](https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/applec/v41y2009i12p1513-1523.html)

# 1. Agregação: compensatória (aditiva) versus não-compensatória (geométrica/MCA)

**Fonte primária:** Nardo, M., Saisana, M., Saltelli, A., Tarantola, S., Hoffman, A., Giovannini, E. (2008). *Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide.* OECD Publishing / European Commission JRC. ISBN 978-92-64-04345-9. Passo 6, secoes 6.10-6.12 (pp. 99-108) e sumario 1.6 (pp. 31-33). Fonte complementar: Munda, G. & Nardo, M. (2009), "Noncompensatory/nonlinear composite indicators for ranking countries: a defensible setting", *Applied Economics* 41(12), 1513-1523 (versao JRC: EUR 21833 EN, 2005).

**Cautelas documentadas (citacoes verbatim do Handbook):**
- Compensabilidade total da agregacao aditiva (p. 103): "an undesirable feature of additive aggregations is the implied full compensability, such that poor performance in some indicators can be compensated for by sufficiently high values in other indicators." Na agregacao linear "the compensability is constant" (p. 33).
- A aditiva exige "preference independence", chamada "a very strong condition", que torna a razao de troca entre variaveis independente das demais - premissa considerada "quite an unrealistic assumption (Funtowicz et al., 1990)" (p. 103).
- A geometrica oferece "some degree of non compensability" e "reward those countries with higher scores" (rewarda perfis equilibrados). Exemplo do proprio Handbook (p. 104): os perfis [21,1,1,1] e [6,6,6,6] tem composto aditivo igual, mas composto geometrico de 2,14 versus 6,00.
- Pesos sao razoes de troca, nao coeficientes de importancia (Tabela 4, nota 4, p. 31, verbatim): "With both linear and geometric aggregations weights are trade-offs and not 'importance' coefficients." E (p. 105): "The use of weights with intensity of preference originates in compensatory multi-criteria methods and gives the meaning of trade-offs to the weights. By contrast, the use of weights with ordinal criterion scores originates in non-compensatory aggregation procedures and gives the weights the meaning of importance coefficients."

**Sensibilidade a valores zero - RESSALVA DE HONESTIDADE:** o Handbook nao traz uma frase unica citavel do tipo "a media geometrica e zero se qualquer componente for zero". Isto e propriedade matematica da forma produto (p. 104) combinada com a normalizacao Min-Max, que mapeia o pior desempenho exatamente a 0 (p. 85). O enunciado canonico explicito desse problema de valor zero esta no UNDP Human Development Report 2010 (que migrou o IDH para media geometrica) - fonte primaria distinta, nao verificada neste levantamento.

**Alternativa/recomendacao:** quando as dimensoes forem igualmente legitimas e nao-substituiveis, "a non-compensatory logic might be necessary" e "neither the linear nor the geometric aggregation are suitable"; recomenda-se uma abordagem multicriterio nao-compensatoria (MCA, procedimentos Condorcet/Borda), que preserva os pesos como coeficientes de importancia e "does not reward outliers, as it retains only ordinal information". Custo documentado: por Arrow & Raynaud (1986), "no perfect aggregation rule may exist" (possiveis ciclos de Condorcet) e o metodo "could be computationally costly when the number of countries is high, as the number of permutations to calculate increases exponentially" (p. 33).

*Nota de sourcing:* o texto proprio de Munda & Nardo nao pode ser transcrito verbatim (PDF do JRC ilegivel via fetch); citacao e resumo verificados, e o argumento e fielmente veiculado no Handbook secao 6.12, que o atribui explicitamente a eles.

# 2. Normalizacao: ranking/percentil versus min-max versus z-score

**Fonte primaria:** Handbook (2008), Passo 5 "Normalisation" (pp. 83-87) e sumario 1.5 (pp. 27-30), Tabela 3 (p. 30) e Tabela 15 (p. 87).

**Cautelas documentadas (verbatim):**
- Ranking (p. 27): "This method is not affected by outliers and allows the performance of countries to be followed over time in terms of relative positions (rankings). Country performance in absolute terms however cannot be evaluated as information on levels is lost." Robusto a outliers, mas descarta niveis absolutos - confirmado.
- Min-Max (p. 28): "extreme values/or outliers could distort the transformed indicator. On the other hand, Min-Max normalisation could widen the range of indicators lying within a small interval, increasing the effect on the composite indicator more than the z-score transformation." Sensivel a outliers e amplia indicadores de baixa variancia - confirmado.
- Z-score (p. 27): "Standardisation (or z-scores) converts indicators to a common scale with a mean of zero and standard deviation of one. Indicators with extreme values thus have a greater effect on the composite indicator." Equaliza a dispersao entre unidades (p. 84: "similar dispersion across countries").

**Alternativa/recomendacao:** o proprio Passo 5 (p. 83) determina que "Different normalisation methods will produce different results for the composite indicator. Therefore, overall robustness tests should be carried out to assess their impact on the outcomes", e recomenda remover outliers antes de normalizar (p. 84). Ou seja, escolher segundo as propriedades dos dados e do objetivo, e submeter a escolha a analise de sensibilidade.

**Ressalvas de fidelidade:**
- A afirmacao de que o ranking "nao mostra se a distancia entre os melhores mudou" NAO esta no Handbook para o metodo de ranking; o texto documenta apenas "information on levels is lost". A dificuldade de acompanhar variacoes ao longo do tempo e documentada para escalas categoricas/percentil, nao para ranking simples.
- O Handbook trata ranking e percentil como metodos distintos (metodo 1 versus metodo 5). O percentil/categorico carrega a cautela adicional de que "exclude large amounts of information about the variance."
- A expressao "unreliable outliers" como limite min/max pertence ao metodo distancia-ao-lider, nao ao min-max.

# 3. CCDF empirica como peso de decaimento versus Kaplan-Meier

**Fonte primaria:** Kaplan, E.L. & Meier, P. (1958), "Nonparametric Estimation from Incomplete Observations", *Journal of the American Statistical Association* 53(282), 457-481. Texto canonico de apoio: Klein, J.P. & Moeschberger, M.L. (2003), *Survival Analysis: Techniques for Censored and Truncated Data*, 2a ed., Springer.

**O que Kaplan-Meier resolve (resumo do abstract):** e um estimador nao-parametrico da funcao de sobrevivencia a partir de observacoes incompletas (censuradas). Assume que "the lifetime (age at death) is independent of the potential loss time" (censura nao-informativa/independente) e estima "the proportion P(t) of items in the population whose lifetimes would exceed t ... without making any assumption about the form of the function P(t)".

**Cautela documentada sobre a CCDF empirica ingenua:** sob censura a direita, a CCDF empirica e viesada e inconsistente - subestima sistematicamente a sobrevivencia (superestima a taxa de eventos / subestima duracoes longas), porque sujeitos ainda "vivos"/em curso no corte tem duracao observada que e apenas um limite inferior, nao o tempo do evento. A construcao produto-limite de KM corrige isso por meio dos conjuntos de risco: unidades censuradas contam em n_i ate seu tempo de censura e depois saem (NIST/SEMATECH Engineering Statistics Handbook). Consequencia para o uso como peso de decaimento: duracoes proximas e alem da janela de observacao ficam subponderadas.

**Cautelas sobre o proprio Kaplan-Meier:** (a) a cauda direita e instavel - vai a 0 se o maior tempo for um evento, ou fica indefinida (plato de massa < 1) acima do maior tempo se este for censurado; logo, pesos derivados da cauda extrema sao pouco confiaveis. (b) Depende do pressuposto de censura nao-informativa/independente.

**Alternativa/recomendacao:** sob censura a direita, usar o estimador produto-limite de Kaplan-Meier, nao a CCDF empirica ingenua.

**Ressalvas de sourcing:** o abstract de KM (1958) foi obtido via indice de busca, nao lido diretamente da pagina tipografica (o PDF primario nao foi extraivel como texto); a redacao e corroborada por multiplas bases de referencia. O reforco explicito de que "the empirical cdf does not provide a consistent estimator ... in the presence of censored data" foi confirmado em fontes secundarias (documentacao lifelines; NIST; arXiv 1310.5927), nao em citacao de pagina de Klein & Moeschberger, que nao pode ser transcrita verbatim.

# 4. Cadencia/churn: Pareto/NBD e BG/NBD

**Fontes primarias:** Schmittlein, D.C., Morrison, D.G., Colombo, R. (1987), "Counting Your Customers: Who Are They and What Will They Do Next?", *Management Science* 33(1), 1-24. Fader, P.S., Hardie, B.G.S., Lee, K.L. (2005), "'Counting Your Customers' the Easy Way: An Alternative to the Pareto/NBD Model", *Marketing Science* 24(2), 275-284.

**Premissas exigidas (verbatim, Fader/Hardie/Lee, restando SMC 1987):** Pareto/NBD assenta em cinco premissas: (i) enquanto ativo, o numero de transacoes segue Poisson com taxa lambda; (ii) heterogeneidade de lambda ~ gama; (iii) cada cliente tem um "lifetime" nao observado, com ponto de inatividade exponencial de taxa mu; (iv) mu ~ gama; (v) lambda e mu independentes entre clientes. O BG/NBD difere apenas na historia de dropout: "if we assume instead that dropout occurs immediately after a purchase" - inatividade com probabilidade p apos cada transacao, p ~ beta.

**Estatisticas suficientes exigidas (verbatim):** "requires only two pieces of information about each customer's past purchasing history: his 'recency' ... and 'frequency' ... The notation ... is (X = x, t_x, T)". Os modelos descrevem "repeat-buying behavior"; na calibracao, x e t_x contam apenas transacoes de repeticao e T e medido a partir da primeira compra.

**Por que exigem historico longo / por que uma janela curta os inviabiliza:** o processo de dropout e nao observado e inferido inteiramente da contagem e do espacamento das transacoes de repeticao. O proprio paper documenta a degradacao no regime esparso (p. 11): "the BG/NBD forecasts tend to be relatively poor when penetration and/or purchase frequency are extremely low"; nos piores casos a frequencia media de compra foi ~1,2. Com frequencia proxima de 1, as estatisticas recencia-frequencia nao separam "ficou inativo" de "ainda ativo, mas ainda nao recomprou".

**Sobre a matriz cliente-produto saturada - INFERENCIA DE APLICABILIDADE (nao afirmada nas fontes):** os modelos operam no grao do cliente (relacionamento) em tempo continuo, sobre todas as compras. Uma matriz cliente-produto com no maximo uma transacao por celula nao fornece sinal algum de temporizacao de recompra por celula (x <= 1, sem intervalo intercompra), colapsando as estatisticas suficientes exatamente no regime de "frequencia extremamente baixa" que o paper aponta como o pior. Isto segue dos requisitos de dados declarados, mas os papers nao tratam do caso cliente-produto - trate como inferencia fundamentada, nao como afirmacao das fontes.

**Ressalvas:** SMC 1987 nao foi obtido em texto integral (paywall); as premissas do Pareto/NBD estao citadas conforme a restatement de Fader/Hardie/Lee (2005). A linguagem "parametros instaveis/nao identificados" e parafrase do achado documentado de degradacao de previsao, nao citacao literal.

---

# 5. Avaliacao de ranqueamento sem verdade-fundamental

**Fontes primarias:** Handbook (2008), tratamento detalhado no Passo 7 "Uncertainty and sensitivity analysis" (pp. 117-131) e sumario 1.7 (p. 34) - rotulado "Step 8" no guia de 10 passos da CE, mesmo conteudo. Saisana, M., Saltelli, A., Tarantola, S. (2005), "Uncertainty and sensitivity analysis techniques as tools for the quality assessment of composite indicators", *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series A* 168(2), 307-323.

**Cautelas documentadas (verbatim):**
- O rank nao e numero robusto (p. 34): "Several judgements have to be made ... The robustness of the composite indicators and the underlying policy messages may thus be contested." Saisana et al. (2005), abstract: "doubts are often raised about the robustness of the resulting countries' rankings and about the significance of the associated policy message." No exemplo TAI (p. 124): "it would have to be concluded that TAI is not a robust measure".
- Sem criterio externo, validar e sobre robustez/consistencia/transparencia, NAO acuracia preditiva (p. 34): "Is the assessment of robustness enough for guaranteeing a sensible composite? Certainly not. We already claimed that a sound theoretical framework is the primary ingredient." O proposito da UA+SA (p. 117): "to gauge the robustness ... to increase its transparency, to identify which countries are favoured or weakened ... and to help frame a debate around the index."

**Recomendacoes (verbatim):**
- Experimento Monte Carlo unico variando todas as fontes de incerteza simultaneamente (p. 117): "The analysis is conducted as a single Monte Carlo experiment ... exploring all uncertainty sources simultaneously". Reportar o rank com bandas de incerteza (p. 34): "country rankings with their related uncertainty bounds ... the plausible range". O exemplo usa mediana e intervalos de 5o-95o percentil dos ranks (Fig. 18, p. 124).
- Analise de sensibilidade baseada em variancia (indices de Sobol de primeira ordem S_i e de efeito total S_Ti, secao 7.3, pp. 121-127), atribuindo a variancia do rank as premissas de entrada: "with non-linear models, robust, 'model-free' techniques should be used ... variance-based techniques are model-free" e distinguem efeitos principais de interacoes.
- Correlacao de ranking (Box 7, pp. 80-81): Spearman "does not require the assumption of normality ... Nor ... an interval scale or a linear association" (testavel por t para n>20); Kendall W "measures the degree of correspondence between two rankings (and the statistical significance)". Apresentadas como ferramentas descritivas de comparacao (contra baselines/sub-indicadores/construcoes alternativas), nao como prova de validacao; a comparacao de robustez principal do Handbook e a distribuicao de ranks (mediana + bandas) mais a estatistica de "average shift in rank" (RS, eq. 38).

**Cautela central:** sem criterio externo, um composto pode ser internamente consistente e robusto e ainda assim nao estar validado contra nenhum desfecho; UA/SA nao estabelece acuracia preditiva. Saisana et al. (2005): a UA/SA contribui para "the indicators' definition of quality and an assessment of the reliability of countries' rankings" e para tornar "policy inference more defensible" e "increase transparency".

**Ressalvas:** de Saisana et al. (2005) so o abstract foi verificavel (texto integral em paywall); citacoes de paginas internas nao sao fornecidas. O intervalo 5o-95o e o metodo do exemplo TAI, nao uma prescricao universal.

---

## Sintese das ressalvas de fidelidade (para nao apresentar como conclusao o que a fonte nao diz)

1. **Zero na media geometrica** (item 1): propriedade matematica implicada, nao frase citavel do Handbook; enunciado canonico no UNDP HDR 2010, nao verificado aqui.
2. **Munda & Nardo** (item 1): abstract e citacao verificados; texto proprio nao transcrito verbatim (PDF ilegivel); argumento veiculado via Handbook secao 6.12.
3. **"Distancia entre os melhores"** (item 2): nao documentado para ranking; o Handbook diz apenas "information on levels is lost".
4. **Kaplan-Meier 1958** (item 3): abstract via indice de busca, nao da pagina tipografica; inconsistencia da CCDF empirica reforcada por fontes secundarias (lifelines, NIST, arXiv), nao por citacao de pagina de Klein & Moeschberger.
5. **Matriz cliente-produto** (item 4): inferencia de aplicabilidade minha, fundamentada nos requisitos de dados declarados; nao afirmada por SMC 1987 nem por Fader/Hardie/Lee 2005. SMC 1987 nao obtido em texto integral.
6. **Saisana et al. 2005** (item 5): apenas o abstract verificavel.

Todas as URLs primarias (Handbook OECD, brucehardie.com para Fader/Hardie/Lee, registros JASA/Management Science/Marketing Science, JRSS-A) foram localizadas e, onde possivel, lidas diretamente do PDF; onde nao foi possivel, esta sinalizado acima.</result>

# 1. Agregação: compensatória (aditiva) versus não-compensatória (geométrica/MCA)

**Fonte primária:** Nardo, M., Saisana, M., Saltelli, A., Tarantola, S., Hoffman, A., Giovannini, E. (2008). *Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide.* OECD Publishing / European Commission JRC. ISBN 978-92-64-04345-9. Passo 6, secoes 6.10-6.12 (pp. 99-108) e sumario 1.6 (pp. 31-33). Fonte complementar: Munda, G. & Nardo, M. (2009), "Noncompensatory/nonlinear composite indicators for ranking countries: a defensible setting", *Applied Economics* 41(12), 1513-1523 (versao JRC: EUR 21833 EN, 2005).

**Cautelas documentadas (citacoes verbatim do Handbook):**
- Compensabilidade total da agregacao aditiva (p. 103): "an undesirable feature of additive aggregations is the implied full compensability, such that poor performance in some indicators can be compensated for by sufficiently high values in other indicators." Na agregacao linear "the compensability is constant" (p. 33).
- A aditiva exige "preference independence", chamada "a very strong condition", que torna a razao de troca entre variaveis independente das demais - premissa considerada "quite an unrealistic assumption (Funtowicz et al., 1990)" (p. 103).
- A geometrica oferece "some degree of non compensability" e "reward those countries with higher scores" (rewarda perfis equilibrados). Exemplo do proprio Handbook (p. 104): os perfis [21,1,1,1] e [6,6,6,6] tem composto aditivo igual, mas composto geometrico de 2,14 versus 6,00.
- Pesos sao razoes de troca, nao coeficientes de importancia (Tabela 4, nota 4, p. 31, verbatim): "With both linear and geometric aggregations weights are trade-offs and not 'importance' coefficients." E (p. 105): "The use of weights with intensity of preference originates in compensatory multi-criteria methods and gives the meaning of trade-offs to the weights. By contrast, the use of weights with ordinal criterion scores originates in non-compensatory aggregation procedures and gives the weights the meaning of importance coefficients."

**Sensibilidade a valores zero - RESSALVA DE HONESTIDADE:** o Handbook nao traz uma frase unica citavel do tipo "a media geometrica e zero se qualquer componente for zero". Isto e propriedade matematica da forma produto (p. 104) combinada com a normalizacao Min-Max, que mapeia o pior desempenho exatamente a 0 (p. 85). O enunciado canonico explicito desse problema de valor zero esta no UNDP Human Development Report 2010 (que migrou o IDH para media geometrica) - fonte primaria distinta, nao verificada neste levantamento.

**Alternativa/recomendacao:** quando as dimensoes forem igualmente legitimas e nao-substituiveis, "a non-compensatory logic might be necessary" e "neither the linear nor the geometric aggregation are suitable"; recomenda-se uma abordagem multicriterio nao-compensatoria (MCA, procedimentos Condorcet/Borda), que preserva os pesos como coeficientes de importancia e "does not reward outliers, as it retains only ordinal information". Custo documentado: por Arrow & Raynaud (1986), "no perfect aggregation rule may exist" (possiveis ciclos de Condorcet) e o metodo "could be computationally costly when the number of countries is high, as the number of permutations to calculate increases exponentially" (p. 33).

*Nota de sourcing:* o texto proprio de Munda & Nardo nao pode ser transcrito verbatim (PDF do JRC ilegivel via fetch); citacao e resumo verificados, e o argumento e fielmente veiculado no Handbook secao 6.12, que o atribui explicitamente a eles.

---

# 2. Normalizacao: ranking/percentil versus min-max versus z-score

**Fonte primaria:** Handbook (2008), Passo 5 "Normalisation" (pp. 83-87) e sumario 1.5 (pp. 27-30), Tabela 3 (p. 30) e Tabela 15 (p. 87).

**Cautelas documentadas (verbatim):**
- Ranking (p. 27): "This method is not affected by outliers and allows the performance of countries to be followed over time in terms of relative positions (rankings). Country performance in absolute terms however cannot be evaluated as information on levels is lost." Robusto a outliers, mas descarta niveis absolutos - confirmado.
- Min-Max (p. 28): "extreme values/or outliers could distort the transformed indicator. On the other hand, Min-Max normalisation could widen the range of indicators lying within a small interval, increasing the effect on the composite indicator more than the z-score transformation." Sensivel a outliers e amplia indicadores de baixa variancia - confirmado.
- Z-score (p. 27): "Standardisation (or z-scores) converts indicators to a common scale with a mean of zero and standard deviation of one. Indicators with extreme values thus have a greater effect on the composite indicator." Equaliza a dispersao entre unidades (p. 84: "similar dispersion across countries").

**Alternativa/recomendacao:** o proprio Passo 5 (p. 83) determina que "Different normalisation methods will produce different results for the composite indicator. Therefore, overall robustness tests should be carried out to assess their impact on the outcomes", e recomenda remover outliers antes de normalizar (p. 84). Ou seja, escolher segundo as propriedades dos dados e do objetivo, e submeter a escolha a analise de sensibilidade.

**Ressalvas de fidelidade:**
- A afirmacao de que o ranking "nao mostra se a distancia entre os melhores mudou" NAO esta no Handbook para o metodo de ranking; o texto documenta apenas "information on levels is lost". A dificuldade de acompanhar variacoes ao longo do tempo e documentada para escalas categoricas/percentil, nao para ranking simples.
- O Handbook trata ranking e percentil como metodos distintos (metodo 1 versus metodo 5). O percentil/categorico carrega a cautela adicional de que "exclude large amounts of information about the variance."
- A expressao "unreliable outliers" como limite min/max pertence ao metodo distancia-ao-lider, nao ao min-max.

---

# 3. CCDF empirica como peso de decaimento versus Kaplan-Meier

**Fonte primaria:** Kaplan, E.L. & Meier, P. (1958), "Nonparametric Estimation from Incomplete Observations", *Journal of the American Statistical Association* 53(282), 457-481. Texto canonico de apoio: Klein, J.P. & Moeschberger, M.L. (2003), *Survival Analysis: Techniques for Censored and Truncated Data*, 2a ed., Springer.

**O que Kaplan-Meier resolve (resumo do abstract):** e um estimador nao-parametrico da funcao de sobrevivencia a partir de observacoes incompletas (censuradas). Assume que "the lifetime (age at death) is independent of the potential loss time" (censura nao-informativa/independente) e estima "the proportion P(t) of items in the population whose lifetimes would exceed t ... without making any assumption about the form of the function P(t)".

**Cautela documentada sobre a CCDF empirica ingenua:** sob censura a direita, a CCDF empirica e viesada e inconsistente - subestima sistematicamente a sobrevivencia (superestima a taxa de eventos / subestima duracoes longas), porque sujeitos ainda "vivos"/em curso no corte tem duracao observada que e apenas um limite inferior, nao o tempo do evento. A construcao produto-limite de KM corrige isso por meio dos conjuntos de risco: unidades censuradas contam em n_i ate seu tempo de censura e depois saem (NIST/SEMATECH Engineering Statistics Handbook). Consequencia para o uso como peso de decaimento: duracoes proximas e alem da janela de observacao ficam subponderadas.

**Cautelas sobre o proprio Kaplan-Meier:** (a) a cauda direita e instavel - vai a 0 se o maior tempo for um evento, ou fica indefinida (plato de massa < 1) acima do maior tempo se este for censurado; logo, pesos derivados da cauda extrema sao pouco confiaveis. (b) Depende do pressuposto de censura nao-informativa/independente.

**Alternativa/recomendacao:** sob censura a direita, usar o estimador produto-limite de Kaplan-Meier, nao a CCDF empirica ingenua.

**Ressalvas de sourcing:** o abstract de KM (1958) foi obtido via indice de busca, nao lido diretamente da pagina tipografica (o PDF primario nao foi extraivel como texto); a redacao e corroborada por multiplas bases de referencia. O reforco explicito de que "the empirical cdf does not provide a consistent estimator ... in the presence of censored data" foi confirmado em fontes secundarias (documentacao lifelines; NIST; arXiv 1310.5927), nao em citacao de pagina de Klein & Moeschberger, que nao pode ser transcrita verbatim.

---

# 4. Cadencia/churn: Pareto/NBD e BG/NBD

**Fontes primarias:** Schmittlein, D.C., Morrison, D.G., Colombo, R. (1987), "Counting Your Customers: Who Are They and What Will They Do Next?", *Management Science* 33(1), 1-24. Fader, P.S., Hardie, B.G.S., Lee, K.L. (2005), "'Counting Your Customers' the Easy Way: An Alternative to the Pareto/NBD Model", *Marketing Science* 24(2), 275-284.

**Premissas exigidas (verbatim, Fader/Hardie/Lee, restando SMC 1987):** Pareto/NBD assenta em cinco premissas: (i) enquanto ativo, o numero de transacoes segue Poisson com taxa lambda; (ii) heterogeneidade de lambda ~ gama; (iii) cada cliente tem um "lifetime" nao observado, com ponto de inatividade exponencial de taxa mu; (iv) mu ~ gama; (v) lambda e mu independentes entre clientes. O BG/NBD difere apenas na historia de dropout: "if we assume instead that dropout occurs immediately after a purchase" - inatividade com probabilidade p apos cada transacao, p ~ beta.

**Estatisticas suficientes exigidas (verbatim):** "requires only two pieces of information about each customer's past purchasing history: his 'recency' ... and 'frequency' ... The notation ... is (X = x, t_x, T)". Os modelos descrevem "repeat-buying behavior"; na calibracao, x e t_x contam apenas transacoes de repeticao e T e medido a partir da primeira compra.

**Por que exigem historico longo / por que uma janela curta os inviabiliza:** o processo de dropout e nao observado e inferido inteiramente da contagem e do espacamento das transacoes de repeticao. O proprio paper documenta a degradacao no regime esparso (p. 11): "the BG/NBD forecasts tend to be relatively poor when penetration and/or purchase frequency are extremely low"; nos piores casos a frequencia media de compra foi ~1,2. Com frequencia proxima de 1, as estatisticas recencia-frequencia nao separam "ficou inativo" de "ainda ativo, mas ainda nao recomprou".

**Sobre a matriz cliente-produto saturada - INFERENCIA DE APLICABILIDADE (nao afirmada nas fontes):** os modelos operam no grao do cliente (relacionamento) em tempo continuo, sobre todas as compras. Uma matriz cliente-produto com no maximo uma transacao por celula nao fornece sinal algum de temporizacao de recompra por celula (x <= 1, sem intervalo intercompra), colapsando as estatisticas suficientes exatamente no regime de "frequencia extremamente baixa" que o paper aponta como o pior. Isto segue dos requisitos de dados declarados, mas os papers nao tratam do caso cliente-produto - trate como inferencia fundamentada, nao como afirmacao das fontes.

**Ressalvas:** SMC 1987 nao foi obtido em texto integral (paywall); as premissas do Pareto/NBD estao citadas conforme a restatement de Fader/Hardie/Lee (2005). A linguagem "parametros instaveis/nao identificados" e parafrase do achado documentado de degradacao de previsao, nao citacao literal.

---

# 5. Avaliacao de ranqueamento sem verdade-fundamental

**Fontes primarias:** Handbook (2008), tratamento detalhado no Passo 7 "Uncertainty and sensitivity analysis" (pp. 117-131) e sumario 1.7 (p. 34) - rotulado "Step 8" no guia de 10 passos da CE, mesmo conteudo. Saisana, M., Saltelli, A., Tarantola, S. (2005), "Uncertainty and sensitivity analysis techniques as tools for the quality assessment of composite indicators", *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series A* 168(2), 307-323.

**Cautelas documentadas (verbatim):**
- O rank nao e numero robusto (p. 34): "Several judgements have to be made ... The robustness of the composite indicators and the underlying policy messages may thus be contested." Saisana et al. (2005), abstract: "doubts are often raised about the robustness of the resulting countries' rankings and about the significance of the associated policy message." No exemplo TAI (p. 124): "it would have to be concluded that TAI is not a robust measure".
- Sem criterio externo, validar e sobre robustez/consistencia/transparencia, NAO acuracia preditiva (p. 34): "Is the assessment of robustness enough for guaranteeing a sensible composite? Certainly not. We already claimed that a sound theoretical framework is the primary ingredient." O proposito da UA+SA (p. 117): "to gauge the robustness ... to increase its transparency, to identify which countries are favoured or weakened ... and to help frame a debate around the index."

**Recomendacoes (verbatim):**
- Experimento Monte Carlo unico variando todas as fontes de incerteza simultaneamente (p. 117): "The analysis is conducted as a single Monte Carlo experiment ... exploring all uncertainty sources simultaneously". Reportar o rank com bandas de incerteza (p. 34): "country rankings with their related uncertainty bounds ... the plausible range". O exemplo usa mediana e intervalos de 5o-95o percentil dos ranks (Fig. 18, p. 124).
- Analise de sensibilidade baseada em variancia (indices de Sobol de primeira ordem S_i e de efeito total S_Ti, secao 7.3, pp. 121-127), atribuindo a variancia do rank as premissas de entrada: "with non-linear models, robust, 'model-free' techniques should be used ... variance-based techniques are model-free" e distinguem efeitos principais de interacoes.
- Correlacao de ranking (Box 7, pp. 80-81): Spearman "does not require the assumption of normality ... Nor ... an interval scale or a linear association" (testavel por t para n>20); Kendall W "measures the degree of correspondence between two rankings (and the statistical significance)". Apresentadas como ferramentas descritivas de comparacao (contra baselines/sub-indicadores/construcoes alternativas), nao como prova de validacao; a comparacao de robustez principal do Handbook e a distribuicao de ranks (mediana + bandas) mais a estatistica de "average shift in rank" (RS, eq. 38).

**Cautela central:** sem criterio externo, um composto pode ser internamente consistente e robusto e ainda assim nao estar validado contra nenhum desfecho; UA/SA nao estabelece acuracia preditiva. Saisana et al. (2005): a UA/SA contribui para "the indicators' definition of quality and an assessment of the reliability of countries' rankings" e para tornar "policy inference more defensible" e "increase transparency".

**Ressalvas:** de Saisana et al. (2005) so o abstract foi verificavel (texto integral em paywall); citacoes de paginas internas nao sao fornecidas. O intervalo 5o-95o e o metodo do exemplo TAI, nao uma prescricao universal.

---

## Sintese das ressalvas de fidelidade (para nao apresentar como conclusao o que a fonte nao diz)

1. **Zero na media geometrica** (item 1): propriedade matematica implicada, nao frase citavel do Handbook; enunciado canonico no UNDP HDR 2010, nao verificado aqui.
2. **Munda & Nardo** (item 1): abstract e citacao verificados; texto proprio nao transcrito verbatim (PDF ilegivel); argumento veiculado via Handbook secao 6.12.
3. **"Distancia entre os melhores"** (item 2): nao documentado para ranking; o Handbook diz apenas "information on levels is lost".
4. **Kaplan-Meier 1958** (item 3): abstract via indice de busca, nao da pagina tipografica; inconsistencia da CCDF empirica reforcada por fontes secundarias (lifelines, NIST, arXiv), nao por citacao de pagina de Klein & Moeschberger.
5. **Matriz cliente-produto** (item 4): inferencia de aplicabilidade minha, fundamentada nos requisitos de dados declarados; nao afirmada por SMC 1987 nem por Fader/Hardie/Lee 2005. SMC 1987 nao obtido em texto integral.
6. **Saisana et al. 2005** (item 5): apenas o abstract verificavel.

Todas as URLs primarias (Handbook OECD, brucehardie.com para Fader/Hardie/Lee, registros JASA/Management Science/Marketing Science, JRSS-A) foram localizadas e, onde possivel, lidas diretamente do PDF; onde nao foi possivel, esta sinalizado acima.</result>

## Cautelas e literatura

As técnicas adotadas foram confrontadas com a literatura estabelecida. As fontes primárias são
citadas e as cautelas registradas; onde uma afirmação é inferência de aplicabilidade ao nosso
caso, e não afirmação da fonte, isto está sinalizado.

- Agregação e compensabilidade. O Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators (OECD/JRC, 2008),
  Passo 6, adverte que a agregação aditiva implica compensabilidade total, na qual o desempenho
  fraco em uma dimensão é compensado por valores altos em outras, e exige independência de
  preferências, tratada como premissa forte e pouco realista. A agregação geométrica ou
  multiplicativa oferece não-compensabilidade parcial e recompensa perfis equilibrados; em ambas,
  os pesos são razões de troca, não coeficientes de importância. Aplicação ao nosso composto: o
  momentum entra multiplicativamente por ser não-substituível, pois o timing errado não deve ser
  compensado por valor ou aderência, o que é o comportamento desejado; a base aditiva de
  econômico, afinidade e aderência é aceitável porque estas são facetas de valor mutuamente
  substituíveis, e os seus pesos são razões de troca. A forma multiplicativa é sensível a valores
  próximos de zero, o que é intencional no fator de momentum, pois um par expirado ou
  recém-fechado deve afundar, e é evitado na base, que é aditiva. A alternativa mais rigorosa, uma
  agregação multicritério não-compensatória (Condorcet ou Borda), é descartada para o MVP pelo
  custo documentado, a inexistência de regra de agregação perfeita (Arrow e Raynaud, 1986) e o
  custo computacional;
- Normalização. O Handbook, Passo 5, documenta que o ranking ou percentil não é afetado por
  outliers mas descarta a informação de nível, que o min-max é distorcido por outliers e amplia
  indicadores de baixa variância, e que a padronização dá peso maior aos valores extremos. Ele
  recomenda testar a robustez entre métodos e remover outliers antes de normalizar. Aplicação: a
  normalização por percentil é adequada ao 'close_value', de cauda longa até cerca de 30.000, ao
  custo de descartar a magnitude absoluta, aceitável para um instrumento de ranqueamento; a
  sensibilidade ao min-max é reportada na validação;
- Peso de decaimento por CCDF empírica. Kaplan e Meier (1958) estabelecem que, sob censura à
  direita, o estimador correto da função de sobrevivência é o produto-limite, e que a CCDF
  empírica ingênua é viesada, pois subestima a sobrevivência ao tratar observações ainda em curso
  como se o evento já tivesse ocorrido. Aplicação: a curva de decaimento é a fração de negócios
  Won com ciclo maior ou igual à idade, calculada sobre negócios já fechados; as oportunidades
  ainda abertas são observações censuradas e a sua exclusão enviesa a curva. Adota-se, ainda
  assim, o proxy empírico pela transparência e comunicabilidade ao vendedor e por não ter
  parâmetro arbitrário, com a ressalva de censura registrada; o corte duro de expiração observado
  na EDA limita a instabilidade da cauda, que também afeta o próprio Kaplan-Meier. A
  inconsistência da CCDF empírica sob censura é corroborada por fontes secundárias de análise de
  sobrevivência, não por citação de página do texto canônico;
- Cadência e churn. Os modelos Pareto/NBD (Schmittlein, Morrison e Colombo, 1987) e BG/NBD
  (Fader, Hardie e Lee, 2005) inferem a inatividade não observada a partir da recência e da
  frequência de compras de repetição, e degradam quando a frequência é muito baixa, próxima de
  um, caso em que a recência e a frequência não separam o cliente inativo do ativo que ainda não
  recomprou. Aplicação, marcada como inferência e não afirmada pelas fontes: a matriz
  cliente-produto saturada, com no máximo uma transação por célula em muitos casos, e a janela de
  cerca de dez meses colocam o problema nesse regime degenerado, o que inviabiliza esses modelos
  e justifica o proxy de cadência simples e a inércia da dimensão de inatividade nesta base;
- Avaliação sem verdade-fundamental. O Handbook, Passo 7, e Saisana, Saltelli e Tarantola (2005)
  estabelecem que, sem critério externo, a validação é sobre robustez, consistência e
  transparência, e não sobre acurácia preditiva, e que um composto pode ser internamente robusto
  sem estar validado contra qualquer desfecho, sendo o arcabouço teórico o ingrediente primário.
  Recomendam um experimento de Monte Carlo variando simultaneamente as fontes de incerteza,
  reportar o ranking com bandas de incerteza (mediana e percentis 5 e 95), a análise de
  sensibilidade baseada em variância e a correlação de ranking (Spearman, Kendall) como
  ferramenta descritiva de comparação, não como prova de validação. A validação da Fase 5 adota
  essa orientação: o arcabouço teórico é a EDA e esta metodologia, e os baselines, a sensibilidade
  e a validade de face medem robustez, não a acurácia, que a EDA já declarou fraca.
